question: How does SearchUnify determine if a piece of text is appropriate for a certain audience?
reference_answer: It evaluates text difficulty by looking at vocabulary, sentence length, syntactic complexity and readability scores, then decides if the text matches the intended reading level.

question: What files are included in the email when a website crawl fails?
reference_answer: The email includes the crawl log and a second file that lists the URLs that could not be crawled.

question: When I run a search, does SearchUnify look at the original content sources?
reference_answer: No, it matches the query against the data stored in its index, which is a processed snapshot of the content sources.

question: How does the Retriever component use entity detection to narrow down results?
reference_answer: Retriever runs Named Entity Recognition on the query, maps detected entities to labels (like Place) and automatically filters results to those matching the entity, so users don’t need to pick facets manually.

question: Which parameters must I provide when calling getCaseDeflectedArticles with the Python SDK?
reference_answer: You must supply startDate (string), endDate (string), searchClientId (string), internalUser (string) and searchType (string). Optional parameters are count (integer) and offset (integer).

question: What role does the Intent Detector play when a user types a query?
reference_answer: The Intent Detector maps the query to trained user intents, allowing admins to configure results that match the top intents and deliver the most relevant content.

question: How can I view the individual actions that occurred during a specific session?
reference_answer: Click the session ID to open a dialog that lists each activity’s type, detail (such as query text or clicked URL), and timestamp; you can sort by the Time column to see the earliest or latest actions first.

question: How do I turn off an LLM connection and stop features like SearchUnifyGPT from working?
reference_answer: Move the Connection toggle to the left to deactivate the connection; you can also click Cancel to clear the API key, which immediately disables SearchUnifyGPT and Summarize Results until a new key is entered and re‑activated.

question: Can I change the size of the Case Summary panel in Agent Helper, and if so, what limits apply?
reference_answer: Yes—drag the handle at the bottom of the panel to resize it between a minimum height of 20% and a maximum of 80%; if you go outside that range it will snap back to the nearest valid size.

question: What are the main steps to install the SearchUnify search client on a Zendesk Guide knowledge base?
reference_answer: First ensure the Help Center is active and the Guide is configured, then download and unzip the client. In Zendesk, open Guide admin, customize, edit code, replace the code in search_results.hbs with index.html, replace the hero‑inner div in home_page.hbs with the autocomplete code, paste the autocomplete scripts at the end of home_page.hbs, and finally publish the changes.

question: How can I use the question‑mark and asterisk wildcards in an advanced search query?
reference_answer: The question mark (?) stands for a single character, so a query like "a?l" matches three‑letter words such as all, awl, or AOL. The asterisk (*) represents any trailing phrase, so "search*" returns words that start with "search", like searches, searching, and searched.

question: What is the mechanism behind Auto Tuning that makes results personal for each user?
reference_answer: Auto Tuning records each user’s search sessions, analyzes the activity to find patterns, and then uses a machine‑learning engine to reorder results based on those patterns. Personalization only occurs when a user’s behavior reaches a similarity threshold with other users, otherwise each user’s results are based solely on their own activity.

question: How do I configure a search client to show results from only one content source?
reference_answer: In the search client settings, enable the "favorite content source" option and select the single source you want the client to query; this limits the client to fetch documents exclusively from that source.

question: What do I need to have ready before I can install a SearchUnify client in ServiceNow?
reference_answer: You must have the Customer Service plug‑in activated in ServiceNow and the SearchUnify user scope set to either "Search" or "All" before starting the installation.

question: Can I turn off Did You Mean suggestions for specific keywords?
reference_answer: Yes, use the new Hide Suggestions feature to disable suggestions for a selected list of keywords while keeping the auto‑correct functionality active for all other terms.

question: How can I retrieve the list of objects and their fields for a specific content source?
reference_answer: Call the endpoint GET contentSource/{id}/objectAndFields, providing the content source ID you obtained from GET contentSource/all. The response returns each object with its id, label, name, and a fields object describing each field’s properties.

question: If I set both a query‑specific boost and a regex boost for the same document, which one wins?
reference_answer: Query‑specific boosting takes precedence over regex‑based boosting, so the query boost will be applied when both exist.

question: How do I change a product name across all indexed fields using the Find and Replace feature?
reference_answer: On the Rules screen click the magnifying‑glass "Find and Replace" button, choose "All" in the Enter Name dropdown, enter the old product name in the Find column and the new name in the Replace column (you can use regex), click Add, then Save and run a crawl to apply the changes to the index.

question: What is the longest search query that the SearchUnify clients will accept?
reference_answer: The maximum query length is 200 characters; longer queries are truncated to this limit.

question: How do I download the SharePoint SearchUnify client package?
reference_answer: After creating a search client and connecting it, go to Search Clients in the main navigation, locate the SharePoint search client, and click the download icon; the client will be downloaded as a zip folder.

question: How can I replace a product name across all indexed fields without changing the original source files?
reference_answer: Use the Find and Replace button on the Rules screen, select "All" in the Enter Name dropdown, enter the old and new product names in the Find and Replace columns, add the rule, save, and then run a crawl to update the search index.

question: What steps do I follow to install a Knowledge Agent I configured in the Agentic Suite onto Salesforce on my own?
reference_answer: Open the deployment screen, click the document icon to view the Salesforce deployment instructions, follow those steps, and then click Save before activating the agent on the Agents List screen.

question: I forgot my SearchUnify password; how do I reset it?
reference_answer: On the login page select Forgot Your Password, enter your User ID, click Send an Email, then use the recovery link sent to your inbox within one hour to set a new password (or contact your admin if you can't answer the security question).

question: How do I request an access token using my client ID and secret via curl?
reference_answer: Send a POST request to http://yourinstance/oauth/token with a Basic authorization header containing the Base64‑encoded clientId:clientSecret, and include grant_type=password, username, and password in the form data.

question: Where can I see if I'm close to exceeding my monthly LLM token quota and when will I be notified?
reference_answer: Check the API Consumption section in LLM Usage Insights, where the usage bar changes color as you approach the limit, and you’ll receive email alerts at 50%, 90%, and 100% consumption, with a CSM contacting you at 90%.

question: How do I call the API to get a content source's object and its fields using the Java SDK?
reference_answer: Create a SearchUnifyClient, build a GetContentSourceObjectAndFieldsRequest with the content source ID, and call client.getContentSourceObjectAndFields(request) to receive the response.

question: Which SearchUnify field stores the ServiceNow knowledge base name?
reference_answer: The SearchUnify field "name" maps to the ServiceNow field kb_knowledge_base (name).

question: Why can't I change the Relevancy tab on the main search client while an A/B test is active?
reference_answer: When an A/B test is running, the Relevancy tab is locked for the main search client; only the sub-search clients (test variants) allow editing of the Relevancy tab.

question: How can I view the queries that caused users to click an article that didn’t deflect a case?
reference_answer: Select the article in the left "Articles Failed to Deflect Cases" section; the right "Searches for Clicked Result" panel will list the queries and the number of times each query was run.

question: What error might occur if I schedule Litmos crawling on the 30th of each month?
reference_answer: If you choose the 30th, the crawler may throw an error in February with the message “Chosen date will not work for this month.”

question: What details are displayed for each entry in the SearchUnifyGPT Error Logs tab?
reference_answer: Each row shows the search query that triggered the error (truncated to 42 characters), the session ID, the time of the search, and the error code returned.

question: How can I protect a web search client by using my existing authentication system with SearchUnify?
reference_answer: Set up middleware so the customer backend validates the user, then forwards the query to the SearchUnify API and returns the results; you need a secure route (e.g., /api/su/search) and the authentication headers required by the SDK.

question: What steps do I follow to add objects and fields when creating an API content source?
reference_answer: Enter the object containing your data, give it a label and click Add Object; repeat for additional objects; click Manage Fields, add the fields you want indexed, click Save, then click Save again for the object.

question: What are the four manual tuning options in SearchUnify and when should each be used?
reference_answer: Intent Tuning boosts documents for large sets of related keywords (over 8); Keyword Tuning boosts for small sets (under 8); Content Tuning personalizes search by boosting content types, content sources, or documents whose field values match the query; Custom Tuning is another manual option not detailed here.

question: Where can I see the list of users who have logged into SearchUnify via SSO?
reference_answer: Go to Administration > Manage Users and open Hosted Search Users; the list populates automatically as employees sign in with single sign‑on.

question: How do I install a SearchUnify search client in my Zendesk Support instance?
reference_answer: First create a Zendesk content source and a Zendesk search client in SearchUnify, then download the client zip. In Zendesk, go to the Admin Center → Apps and Integrations → Zendesk Support Apps > Private Apps, click Upload Private App, give it a name, choose the zip file and upload. Confirm the pop‑up, optionally set role or group restrictions, click Install, and verify the client appears under the Currently Installed tab.

question: Why can an admin crawl a Confluence space but still not see hidden pages that a regular user can’t find?
reference_answer: SearchUnify respects both space and page permissions, with page permissions taking precedence. An admin with view access to a space will crawl all pages except any that are hidden at the page level, and users cannot see those hidden pages even if they have space access.

question: What actions are available to me under the Manage Users section of the admin console?
reference_answer: In Manage Users you can add or delete a user, change a user’s role or API/SDK scope, configure SAML 2.0 login, view hosted search users from an identity provider, and (for Super Admins) set access control settings for admins and moderators.

question: How can I preview the effect of my search tuning settings before they go live?
reference_answer: Use the Test Your Tuning feature, which simulates your search client’s behavior and lets you compare boosted results with normal results and with the current live results.

question: What information does the Search Filter Based Clicks report provide about where users are clicking?
reference_answer: The report shows which content sources receive the most clicks, the most common content types used as filters within each source, and the most selected content fields and field values, letting you map these to the corresponding facets on your search client.

question: Why is the Choose a Date option disabled when setting up a Skilljar content source?
reference_answer: The Choose a Date feature is grayed out because each crawl indexes all data from scratch; you set the crawl frequency after configuring the source and simply click Set.

question: How can I share a knowledge‑base article with a customer without opening a separate search client?
reference_answer: Use the Top Related Articles section in the Agent Helper console; it lists relevant articles and lets you share them directly with the customer.

question: How do I turn on the ability to search for symbols like +, *, or @ in a search client?
reference_answer: Edit the search client, open the Relevancy tab, toggle on Special Characters Search, and save the settings.

question: Can I test CSS changes to my Imperium search client without affecting the live site?
reference_answer: Yes, the new Search Client Editor lets admins upload CSS and use the Preview button to experiment without impacting production.

question: What does the metric IDVG represent in session analytics?
reference_answer: IDVG is the Implicit Deflection Volume attributed to user resolutions achieved through interactions with the SearchUnifyGPT AI assistant.

question: How can I hide the main navigation on a small screen and then bring it back?
reference_answer: Click the Navigation icon in the menu bar to collapse the navigation; to restore it, hover over the collapsed area and click the Navigation icon again.

question: What does LIME do for machine‑learning predictions?
reference_answer: LIME explains any classifier’s predictions in a human‑understandable way by locally approximating the model with an interpretable one, such as a linear model, showing which features drive a specific prediction.

question: Where can I find the options to deploy the AI Escalation Manager in Salesforce?
reference_answer: The deployment options are listed under Managing Agents → Deploying Agents → Deploy AI Escalation Manager: Installation in Salesforce Service Console.

question: What is coreference resolution and why is it important?
reference_answer: Coreference resolution identifies when different expressions refer to the same entity, which is essential for understanding entity relationships and maintaining coherence in language‑understanding tasks.

question: What metric shows how often AI‑generated responses were copied by agents?
reference_answer: The metric is "Response Assist Copy (%)", which reports the number and percentage of times the generated responses were copied.

question: How do I sign up for the SearchUnify Community?
reference_answer: Go to https://community.searchunify.com, click Register, fill in your full name and email, then click Sign Up. Check your email for the confirmation link, follow it, set a password, and you’ll be registered.

question: What does SearchUnify do to tokens during indexing regarding case and stopwords?
reference_answer: During indexing, SearchUnify removes all stopwords and punctuation and converts the remaining tokens to lowercase.

question: What’s the main difference between keyword search and neural search in SearchUnify?
reference_answer: Keyword search matches exact keywords or phrases and lacks contextual understanding, while neural search uses deep‑learning models to understand the context and semantics of queries.

question: If I set the crawl schedule to a specific day of the month, what should I avoid and why?
reference_answer: Avoid choosing the 30th because the crawler may error in February with the message “Chosen date will not work for this month.” It’s recommended to pick a date between the 1st and 28th.

question: When can I see detailed admin logs for changes made to content sources?
reference_answer: Detailed admin logs for content sources are available only in the Q2 ’25 and later releases and capture actions like adding, editing, deleting sources, authentication changes, crawl frequency updates, rule edits, annotation changes, and crawl start/stop events.

question: How is the Relevance Index calculated and what weights are used for each factor?
reference_answer: The Relevance Index combines three weighted factors: Conversions (40% weight), Average Click Position (30% weight, normalized before use), and Query Match (30% weight). Each factor is calculated from search activity and then multiplied by its weight, and the weighted values are summed to produce the final index.

question: Which objects can I index from GetGuru and how do I select them?
reference_answer: Only Cards, the knowledge articles, are supported for indexing. In the GetGuru connector you use the "By Content Types" tab to view the Cards object and its fields, then switch to the "By Collections" subtab to pick specific cards from the alphabetical list before saving the settings.

question: What are the best practices for using ordered lists so that ML Workbench can extract rich snippets?
reference_answer: Place essential information in the first three to four bullets, keep each bullet under 80 characters, and ensure the most important list appears first if multiple lists exist. ML Workbench extracts from <ol> ordered lists only, not from unordered lists.

question: What steps must I follow to grant the required Apex class access for the SearchUnify AI Support Agent in a Salesforce community?
reference_answer: In Setup, open All Sites, edit the target community's Builder profile, go to Enabled Apex Class Access, edit, move su_agenticsuite.SUAuthentication from Available to Enabled Apex Classes, and save the changes.

question: What recent documentation updates were made in June 2025 regarding user filters and the Relevance Index report?
reference_answer: In June 2025, information about user filters was added to the Relevance Index report, and domain restrictions were removed on preview search results and configuring content sources (preview results).

question: How can I copy all my keyword boosting settings from one search client to another?
reference_answer: In the new release, an admin can copy all keyword boosting settings from one search client to another with a single click of a button.

question: What defines a search conversion in the analytics reports?
reference_answer: A search conversion occurs whenever a user performs a search and clicks on at least one result; if no result is clicked, it is not a conversion.

question: When will the Re‑Connect button be shown for a Stack Overflow for Teams content source?
reference_answer: The Re‑Connect button appears when the authentication details have changed or the authentication fails, requiring the admin to re‑authenticate the source.

question: How can I sort the case lists in the Escalation Predictor reports?
reference_answer: The Cases Likely to Escalate list can be sorted by Created Date or Updated Date, and the Escalated Cases list can be sorted by Created Date or Escalated Date, each with a selectable date range.

question: What does the Live Search Stream widget display?
reference_answer: Live Search Stream shows the real‑time locations of users across your search clients, updating automatically.

question: Can I set a custom date range longer than a month for the API Consumption report?
reference_answer: No, a custom period cannot exceed 30 days.

question: What do I need to do for SearchUnify to crawl my on‑premise Jira instance?
reference_answer: Contact your SearchUnify support rep to get a list of IP addresses that must be whitelisted on your Jira server, then SearchUnify will be able to crawl the data.

question: Where can I view intent usage statistics for my virtual agents?
reference_answer: Open the Virtual Agents interface and scroll right to the Analytics tab, which shows a table of the most frequently encountered intents.

question: Why are some content source edit buttons greyed out for me as a moderator?
reference_answer: Moderators and admins can only edit or delete content sources and search clients they own; items they don’t own appear greyed out and the Total Documents count is unclickable.

question: Can I run an A/B test on a search client to see which search type performs best?
reference_answer: Yes, you can run A/B testing on a Search Client to compare Keyword, Neural, or Hybrid search types and measure which yields higher CTR, ACP, and deflection.

question: Which KPIs tell me about case volume versus timeliness in the escalation analytics?
reference_answer: Open Cases and Open Escalations indicate volume, while Avg. age of Escalated Cases and Avg. age of Escalation Duration indicate timeliness.

question: How do I hide specific facets or all facets in a search client?
reference_answer: Click Hide Facets, then check the facets you want to remove, or select Hide All Facets to remove every facet; the selected facets will no longer appear for users.

question: What should I do if I need expert assistance with an issue?
reference_answer: You can contact your Customer Success Manager or submit a support case via the Submit a Support Case link; you’ll be able to track the case progress there.

question: How can I sort the list of escalated cases by creation or escalation date?
reference_answer: In the Escalated Cases section, select a date range for Created Date or Escalated Date to sort and view cases within that period.

question: How can I see which documents are boosted for a specific intent in a search client?
reference_answer: Go to Search Tuning > Manual, select the search client, enable Boost Document for Intent, then click Boosted Documents to view the list of intent‑boosted documents.

question: What steps do I follow to group similar facets together in a search client?
reference_answer: Open the search client’s edit settings, go to Content Sources, open Merge Facets, drag a facet from the Facets column to Selected Facets, click the facet, Add Filters, create a subgroup name, choose whether child facets are shown, and then Save twice.

question: What is reward modeling in reinforcement learning and how does it differ from using only win/loss rewards?
reference_answer: Reward modeling creates a model that predicts human‑defined rewards for intermediate actions, guiding the AI toward desired outcomes, whereas traditional RL relies solely on final win or loss signals.

question: How do I configure the SearchUnify Chrome extension to use my own search URL?
reference_answer: After adding the extension from the Chrome Web Store, open it from Extensions, enter the base part of your search URL (the text between https:// and ?searchString=) in the "Please Enter the Query URL" field, and click Save.

question: What are the three tuning options an admin can use to influence document ranking?
reference_answer: Admins can use Keyword Tuning to assign specific ranks to documents for queries, Content Source Tuning to boost all documents in a source, and Field Tuning to adjust the weight of fields like title, status, age, and popularity.

question: How can I duplicate an existing search client and give it a new name for a different platform?
reference_answer: In the admin panel go to Search Clients, locate the client you want to copy and click the clone icon. Enter a new label for the clone, choose the target platform (e.g., Salesforce, Khoros, or Website) from the Select Search Client dropdown, and then click Clone. The new client gets a new UID but retains all configurations, content sources, and tuning settings of the original.

question: Is it possible to email an analytics report that contains data from more than two years ago?
reference_answer: No. The Send via Email filter only works for data up to two years prior (e.g., in 2025 you can send data back to 2023). The available reports with this filter are Tiles in Overview, Average Click Position, Case Deflection Trend Chart in Conversions, Tiles in Content Gap Analysis, and Search Summary.

question: Which case fields must be indexed for the Escalation Predictor to function?
reference_answer: Escalation Predictor requires the following fields to be indexed: Owner Name, Contact Name, ID, Case Number, Created Date, Closed Date, Contact Email, Last Modified Date, Case Origin, Escalation, Subject, Status, Description, and Priority.

question: How do I change a product name in all indexed fields using the Higher Logic Vanilla source?
reference_answer: Open the Rules screen, click the Find and Replace button, select "All" (or a specific field) in the Enter Name dropdown, enter the old product name in the Find column and the new name in the Replace column, click Add, then Save and run a crawl so the updated values appear in search results.

question: What scores are combined to produce the overall Case Quality Score?
reference_answer: The Case Quality Score averages the following ten parameters: Sentiment Score, Compliance & Security Adherence Score, Case Documentation Quality Score, Resolution Accuracy Score, Technical Analysis Score, Response SLA Score, Resolution SLA Score, Response Quality Score, Issue Comprehension Rating, and Customer Engagement.

question: How long should I run an A/B test to get reliable results?
reference_answer: Run the test for 7–14 days to ensure enough traffic for reliable results.

question: How can I retrieve my Guru username and user token for SearchUnify authentication?
reference_answer: Log into Guru, go to Team Settings → Users and Collections to see your username, then open Apps and Integrations → API Access, generate a user token for the selected user, copy the token and use it in SearchUnify.

question: Is it possible to make Adobe Assets files searchable in SearchUnify?
reference_answer: Yes, the new Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) content source lets you connect SearchUnify to Adobe Assets folders, indexing files that become searchable by file title, URL, tag, and other properties.

question: What are the steps to configure hosted SSO (SAML 2.0) for SearchUnify?
reference_answer: Go to Hosted SSO Configuration, select an application, enter the IdP SSO and logout URLs, upload or paste the .pem certificate, provide the Hosted Search Client URL, toggle Activate SSO on, and save.

question: How do I create a new intent from a suggested intent in the NLP manager?
reference_answer: Select the suggested intent, click the three‑dot Action menu and choose Move Intent, give the new intent a name, and click Move; associated utterances are moved automatically.

question: How do I add a Wistia content source and choose the authentication method?
reference_answer: Go to Content Sources, click Add New Content Sources, find Wistia and click Add. Give it a name, select OAuth or API as the authentication type, choose the data language, and then click Connect.

question: What’s the process for starting a new discussion on the SearchUnify community?
reference_answer: Log in at https://community.searchunify.com, scroll to the Discussions section, click Start a Discussion, fill in a short title, detailed description (you can add images or links), select Discussion as the topic, and then click Submit.

question: What information do I need before I can create a trial or subscription account in SearchUnify?
reference_answer: You need an Account ID (usually the email used for the trial or purchase), a Password, the Endpoint URL of your instance (e.g., https://mycompany.searchunify.com), and a 60‑character Provision Key.

question: When adding LearnUpon as a content source, what authentication options are available and what credentials do they require?
reference_answer: You can choose Basic authentication, which needs the API Key and API Secret, or OAuth authentication, which requires the Client ID and Client Secret.

question: How can I set up the Apex class and trigger so closed cases are sent to the Case Quality Agent?
reference_answer: Create a new Apex class named CaseQualityTesting with a @future callout method that posts the case ID to the SearchUnify webhook URL, then add a trigger on the Case object (after update) that calls this method when the Status changes to 'Closed'.

question: Where can I configure session timeout and other analytics properties for a search client?
reference_answer: Go to Search Clients > Edit > Analytics Settings and use the Analytics Properties section, which includes Session Timeout and many other options.

question: How can I see who submitted an annotation request and when it was made?
reference_answer: Open the Annotation Re‑Submission History button on the right side of the panel; it shows the Requester and Timestamp for each request.

question: Can I replace all instances of my old product name with the new one in the index without changing the source data?
reference_answer: Yes—use the Find and Replace button on the Rules tab, choose “All” (or a specific field), enter the old name in Find and the new name in Replace, add, save and run a crawl to apply the changes to the index.

question: How do I set a Salesforce content source to crawl every eight hours?
reference_answer: After the first crawl, edit the source, set Choose a Date, select Hours for Frequency, then pick 8 from the dropdown; the source will crawl every eight hours.

question: Why am I seeing fewer indexed URLs than the total URLs listed in my sitemap?
reference_answer: The crawler only indexes text files; non‑text files like PNGs are skipped, so if many URLs point to such files the indexed count will be lower.

question: How can I set up email subscriptions for analytics reports and choose how often I receive them?
reference_answer: Go to Administration > Alerts, open Analytics Subscription and click Add Subscription. Enter the subscriber email addresses separated by commas and pick Daily, Weekly or Monthly as the email frequency, then save the settings.

question: What kinds of feedback can end users give on the search page?
reference_answer: Users can either give a simple rating of their search experience, or they can give a rating plus an optional text comment. All feedback is stored in the Search Experience Feedback report.

question: What is the curl request to exchange a refresh token for a new access token?
reference_answer: Use a POST to {{hostname}}/oauth/token with headers: authorization (base64‑encoded clientId:clientSecret), cache-control set to no-cache, and content-type set to application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Include form data grant_type=refresh_token and refresh_token=<your refresh token>.

question: How do I add page‑view and search analytics to a custom SearchUnify search interface?
reference_answer: Insert the an.js script tag (<script src="<client_url>/resources/Allow/an.js?uid=<uid>"></script>) into the page header to capture page‑view data, and call gza("search",{searchString:...,result_count:...,page_no:...,uid:...,filter:...}) each time a search response is returned to record search analytics.

question: What steps are required to configure the Agent Helper app for the Salesforce Service Console?
reference_answer: In the Apps section, open Agent Helper, click Add New Configuration, choose Salesforce, select your Salesforce search client, then pick a content source and fields. Optionally set different search clients for "search" and "Citation Search", click Next, skip Data Conditions if desired, and complete the configuration. Use the toggle to enable or disable the app afterwards.

question: How can I obtain the SP Issuer value needed for the Okta SAML configuration?
reference_answer: Multitenant customers should contact the SearchUnify support team to get the SP Issuer value.

question: How do I change the default SearchUnify login URL to use my own domain?
reference_answer: Use the Domain mapping option in the Security section to replace the default URL (yourcompany.searchunify.com) with your custom domain (e.g., xyz.yourcompany.com).

question: What curl command should I run to get access and refresh tokens on the Q2 ’25 release?
reference_answer:
Run:
```
curl -i -X POST 'http://yourinstance/oauth/token' \
  -H "authorization: Basic Base64(clientId: clientSecret)" \
  -H 'cache-control: no-cache' \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'grant_type=client_credentials'
```

question: What error might I see if I schedule a Khoros crawl on the 30th of each month?
reference_answer: If you choose the 30th, the crawler may throw an error in February saying “Chosen date will not work for this month.”

question: How long does a refresh token remain valid when using the Search API?
reference_answer: A refresh token is valid for 14 days.

question: How do I set up the source and destination content sources for the Knowledge Graph in a search client?
reference_answer: Go to Search Clients → Edit → Knowledge Graph → Metadata Graph and click Add Relation. Enter a relation name, pick the search client, choose the source content source and (usually) the same destination content source, then click Add Relation to save.

question: Where can I view the Advertisement Performance Report and what columns does it contain?
reference_answer: Open Search Analytics → Overview and scroll down to the Advertisement Performance Report section. The report shows three columns: Search Text (the ad’s search phrase), Appearances (impressions), and Clicks (number of clicks).

question: What do I need to do to start using SearchUnify REST APIs for the first time?
reference_answer: Create an app to obtain a client ID and client secret, then generate an access token and a refresh token (e.g., via curl or Postman). The refresh token lets you request new access tokens for API calls.

question: How can I boost documents whose titles contain certain keywords on a search client?
reference_answer: Enable Custom Boosting on the desired search client, turn on the Title boost (you may need to request it from your SearchUnify representative), set a multiplier greater than 1 for the Title field, and the relevance score of title‑matching documents will increase accordingly.

question: How do I add a new entity and its values in the Taxonomy section of NLP Manager?
reference_answer: In NLP Manager, click Taxonomy, then Add Entity. Enter the entity name and list its values (each value becomes a tag). Save the entity to create the cluster of tags.

question: How can I enable the virtual agent inside my SearchUnify instance?
reference_answer: Toggle the Help Link or Bot switch to the right in User Settings to use a virtual agent directly inside the instance.

question: Which SearchUnify field should I select to index the Khoros field called "current_revision"?
reference_answer: Select the "last_update_time" field in SearchUnify when choosing Khoros fields for indexing.
